title: Motion Creative Analytics vs Sprites: Which Fits Your Team?
summary: Motion and Sprites both analyse creative and both launch ads. Channels, features and 2026 pricing compared from each vendor’s own published pages.
body_markdown:
**Motion and Sprites both analyse ad creative, and since June 2026 both launch ads too, so the choice is not analysis against execution.** It comes down to four things: which channels each one runs, where its analysis starts, how much control you keep over what goes live, and what it costs.


*Last reviewed September 7, 2026. Every Motion fact below comes from Motion’s own published pages, cited and dated. Sprites makes this comparison, so read the Motion column as the vendor’s own description and check it yourself.*


## First, which Motion


There are two well-known products called Motion, and search results mix them constantly. **Motion the creative analytics platform is[motionapp.com](https://motionapp.com/)** . Motion the AI task-and-calendar assistant is usemotion.com — a different company in a different category. Motion’s own reference page opens with the same disambiguation. This comparison is about motionapp.com, whose ads you can read at[Motion (Creative Analytics) in the ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library/motion-creative-analytics) ; the calendar app’s ads are filed separately, because both advertise from a Facebook page called exactly “Motion”.


## What changed in 2026


Most comparisons of these two products rest on a distinction that no longer holds. Motion used to analyse and brief, and stop there. On **June 24, 2026** it shipped[Runneth](https://runneth.com/) , an AI marketing agent that runs on a per-customer virtual machine, lives in Slack and connects to the rest of your stack. Runneth’s own site shows it being told to “launch these ads into the Speaker Statics adset inside of our CSS 2026 campaign”, designing and publishing landing pages, and reporting back that “you launched 22 creatives so far this week”.


So Motion executes. Anything describing it as reporting-only was written before the middle of 2026, and this page said so itself in an earlier draft. Two caveats Motion states in its own words: Runneth requires a Motion subscription and ships deliverables from the Pro plan, and its FAQ answers the question “It just launched, so is it actually proven?” — fair to weigh against the longer track record on the analytics side.


## What Motion is


Motion describes itself as “the command-center for creative and performance teams” and reports[2,100+ customers who analysed more than $14 billion in ad spend last year](https://motionapp.com/llm-info) . Three parts:


- **Creative analytics.** Connect Meta, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn ad accounts; Motion groups creatives automatically and builds top-performing, comparative and launch-analysis reports. Naming conventions and AI tags across eight categories supply the dimensions you filter on. Snapshots share a frozen or live report with people who have no platform access.
- **Inspo.** Creative research: follow other advertisers, watch their new ads in a feed, save what you like into boards, and run AI tasks over a brand you are tracking.
- **Runneth.** The agent layer added in June 2026: briefs, hooks, static images, reports, routines and launched ads, driven from Slack.


It is a coherent product for a specific buyer: a team with a creative department, where what is being bought is making creative performance visible to the people who make the creative — and now acting on it.


## What Sprites is


[Sprites](https://www.sprites.ai/) is a marketing agent rather than a reporting surface with an agent attached. The[creative analytics](https://www.sprites.ai/creative-analytics) it does is one stage of a loop: it reads your ad accounts and the public ad libraries, writes the hooks, angles and scripts, builds the campaign, launches the test and reports on what it learned — with every change waiting for your approval before it touches an account. It runs Google, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok and Reddit, and the same agent also handles SEO and AI-visibility work.


The research input differs too. Sprites reads the public ad libraries directly — the[ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) holds 84 advertisers and roughly 67,700 ads across Meta, Google and LinkedIn as of September 7, 2026 — and mines Reddit, Instagram and YouTube for the language the audience actually uses, so a first analysis does not depend on having a creative history of your own to read.


## Side by side


Motion Sprites


Ad platforms Meta, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn. No search. Google, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit. Search and social.


Analysis Automatic creative grouping, AI tags across eight categories, top-performing, comparative and launch-analysis reports. Hook, angle, format and fatigue analysis across your accounts, plus run-length analysis of competitors from the public ad libraries.


Where the analysis starts Your connected ad accounts, plus brands you follow in Inspo. Your accounts and the public Meta, Google and LinkedIn libraries, read directly.


Creative production Runneth ships briefs, hooks, static images and reports, from the Pro plan. Headlines, image concepts and video scripts through the[ad generator](https://www.sprites.ai/ad-generator) .


Launching campaigns Yes, through Runneth, from Slack. Closed-loop pipelines are a Growth-plan engagement built with Motion. Yes, on every plan, and each change is gated on your approval before it goes live.


Attribution integrations Northbeam and Google Analytics 4. Reads the ad platforms and Shopify directly; no Northbeam integration.


Sharing with clients Snapshots: frozen or live reports viewable without platform access. Reports and documents in-app; white-label reporting on the Scale plan.


Beyond paid ads Paid social creative only. SEO, AEO and AI-visibility work run by the same agent.


Track record Creative analytics since 2021; the agent layer since June 2026. Agent-first from the start.


## Pricing


Motion’s pricing page, captured September 7, 2026. Plans are gated on monthly ad spend rather than on seats. Motion Sprites


Entry plan Starter, $750/mo, up to $50k monthly ad spend Build, $149/mo


Mid plan Pro, $1,200/mo, over $50k monthly ad spend Launch, $495/mo


Top plan Growth, on request Grow $985/mo; Scale on request


Free option 14-day trial, no credit card Free tools and the ads library, no account needed


Motion’s prices are from its[pricing page](https://www.motionapp.com/pricing) on September 7, 2026; Sprites’ are on[our pricing page](https://www.sprites.ai/pricing) . They are not priced on the same axis — Motion charges against the ad spend it analyses, Sprites against the agents, credits and workspaces you use — so a spend-heavy account narrows the gap and a lean one widens it. One thing to check before comparing the numbers: Motion’s spend thresholds are published in more than one place and do not always agree between them, so confirm yours in a quote rather than from a page.


## Choose Motion if


- You have a creative department, and the work being bought is making creative performance visible to the people who make the creative.
- You need report types built specifically for creative review — comparative analysis across funnel stages, products, creators or formats — and you will use them weekly.
- You rely on Northbeam or GA4 attribution and want the creative view sitting on top of it.
- You share creative performance with clients or execs who should not have ad-account access.
- Your spend is concentrated in paid social, so a tool with no search coverage costs you nothing.


## Choose Sprites if


- You run search as well as social. Google and Reddit sit outside Motion’s supported platforms, and for many accounts that is where half the budget lives.
- You want the competitor research, the creative generation and the campaign management in one agent rather than three subscriptions.
- You want every change proposed and gated on your approval rather than executed from a chat message.
- You are replacing agency or freelance hours rather than adding a dashboard alongside them.
- SEO and AI visibility are part of the same job and you would rather not buy a second tool for them.


## Honest caveats


Two, in both directions. Sprites is not a visual creative reporting suite: if what you want is the most polished creative dashboard for a creative team to live in every day, Motion is further along that road and it would be silly to pretend otherwise. And the reporting-versus-execution framing that used to flatter Sprites in this comparison is gone — Motion executes now, and a comparison leaning on a distinction the vendor removed a quarter ago is not worth reading.


What survives is narrower and more useful: channel coverage, where the analysis starts, and whether you want an approval gate in front of every change. If those point your way, start with the free research in the[ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) , read[what creative analytics is](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/what-is-creative-analytics) for the underlying method, or[book a demo](https://www.sprites.ai/book-demo) and watch the loop run against your own account.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is Motion creative analytics?


Motion (motionapp.com) is a creative analytics platform for creative and performance teams. It connects Meta, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn ad accounts, groups your creatives automatically, applies AI tags, and builds visual reports — top-performing, comparative and launch-analysis — that pair the creative with the metrics. Motion describes itself as the command-center for creative and performance teams, and reports 2,100+ customers analysing more than $14 billion in ad spend a year.


### Is Motion the same as the Motion calendar app?


No, and the confusion is common enough that Motion publishes a disambiguation line of its own. Motion the creative analytics platform is motionapp.com. Motion the AI task and calendar assistant is usemotion.com, a different company in a different category. Both advertise from a Facebook page called exactly "Motion", which is why the Sprites ads library keeps them as two separate advertisers.


### Does Motion launch ads, or only report on them?


It launches them now. Motion shipped Runneth on June 24, 2026: an AI marketing agent on a per-customer virtual machine that lives in Slack, and Runneth’s own site shows it launching ads into a named ad set, building landing pages and reporting what launched. Anything written before mid-2026 describing Motion as reporting-only is out of date. Runneth ships deliverables from the Pro plan and requires a Motion subscription.


### How much does Motion cost?


Motion’s pricing page on September 7, 2026 lists Starter at $750 a month for brands spending up to $50k a month on ads, Pro at $1,200 a month for brands spending over $50k, and Growth on request. Motion also documents a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. Sprites is priced on agents and workspaces rather than on the ad spend it analyses: Build $149, Launch $495 and Grow $985 a month, with Scale on request.


### What does Sprites do that Motion does not?


Two things. It runs search as well as paid social — Google and Reddit are outside the platforms Motion supports — and the same agent also does SEO and AI-visibility work. It also starts its research outside your account: Sprites reads the public ad libraries directly, so the first analysis does not depend on your own creative history.


### What does Motion do that Sprites does not?


Visual creative reporting built for a creative department, in more depth than Sprites offers: automatic creative grouping, AI tags across eight categories, comparative and launch-analysis report types, and shareable Snapshots that need no platform access. It also integrates Northbeam and Google Analytics 4 attribution, which Sprites does not.


### Can you use both?


Yes, and for a large in-house creative team it is a reasonable setup: Motion as the reporting surface the creative department lives in, Sprites as the agent covering search and SEO alongside paid social. The overlap is larger than it used to be — both ship creative and both launch ads — so the honest question is whether two subscriptions earn their keep against one.
